comment: Records Route 53 holds that Cloudflare does not, on purpose (`add`, created by this stack), and names other stacks own (`allow`, each with its `owner`). zone_diff.py reads both; cf_export.py marks exported records on an `allow` name as replaced_by its owner, so this stack never writes a record set another stack writes. Values here are not secret.

add.reason: only Amazon (ACM) may issue certificates for the domain once Route 53 is authoritative; no wildcard certificates

null MX (RFC 7505): the domain receives no mail as far as public DNS showed on 2026-11-24 (and asks.yaml cloudflare-mail-and-ruleset); dropped automatically if the export (Cloudflare Email Routing) or extra_records carries a real MX

no server sends mail as the apex today; dropped automatically if the export or extra_records carries another SPF (one SPF record per name, RFC 7208). SES sends with MAIL FROM bounce.marisstella.app, which has its own SPF (email stack)

allow.reason: site stack: CloudFront alias for the apex

allow.name: www
allow.reason: site stack: CloudFront alias, 301 to the apex (www is NXDOMAIN on Cloudflare)
site stack: ACM certificate validation records (also copied into Cloudflare before the nameserver change)

allow.name: _*.www
allow.reason: site stack: ACM validation for www

allow.name: _*.grants
allow.reason: site stack: ACM validation for grants

allow.name: _dmarc
allow.reason: email stack (platform/aws/stacks/email, PR 18749): DMARC for the apex, policy raised from none by that stack

allow.name: *._domainkey
allow.reason: email stack: SES Easy DKIM for marisstella.app

allow.name: *._domainkey.news
allow.reason: email stack: SES Easy DKIM for news.marisstella.app

allow.name: bounce
allow.reason: email stack: SES custom MAIL FROM

allow.name: bounce.news
allow.reason: email stack: SES custom MAIL FROM for news.
